task: Everything depends on your talent, <Ranger>! Hold the pencil...oh, no, not like that... it should be like this... Here's your paper. Now, draw something. Ready? Let's see! Aren't you ashamed of yourself? You, the greatest hero of all times, drawing such an obscenity! Well...at least you can draw. There's going to be a drawing competition soon on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> galaxy. But, as you may have already guessed, something bad has happened to our artist. He fell into a canyon while drawing a sketch. His hands are broken now, so he can't participate in the competition. We had no idea what to do! Then we saw you, someone with real talent, at the top of the rangers' ranking. Would you like to become a competitor representing planet <FromPlanet>? It's as easy as ABC! All you have to do is take first place! Think it over. We'll pay you up to <Money> cr. If you agree, you'll have <Day> days to get to the venue.
success:
Congratulations! That was brilliant! You won! Fantastic! Did you know that your paintings were auctioned off? The planet <ToPlanet>'s state museum bought them for almost 100,000,000 cr.! We're going to pay your <Money> cr. out of this very money. Why so sad? There's nothing that can be done about it! You gave the paintings as a present. 
Anyway, call us from time to time. Maybe we'll find another job for you.
loc.1.0: You land at planet <ToPlanet>'s spaceport in the evening. It must have been very crowded here earlier in the afternoon - at least there are a lot of empty bottles, trash, and paper littered about. You walk around the spaceport for a long time. Finally, you find the peleng who was to meet you. You didn't notice him right away, because he's been sleeping all the while on a bench, using a sign with your name on it as a pillow. You wake him up and he takes you to his gravicar.
loc.2.0: As you walk together to the gravicar, the peleng asks, "Do you have any questions about the competition?
loc.2.1:
You'll have three rivals: <clr>Leonid Khmelev<clrEnd>, a rather mediocre artist who usually tries to produce realistic pictures. <clr>Roo-bel<clrEnd> is a very original gaalian artist who paints in a distinctive style. And your most serious opponent is <clr>the peleng Kasyak<clrEnd>. He's a drug-addict, but he can produce real masterpieces when he's high."
"Any more questions?" asks the peleng.
loc.2.2:
"The competition has three judges. The first is a <clr>gaal named Leevi-taan<clrEnd>, a very famous <clr>realist artist<clrEnd>. The second is a <clr>human named Satimov<clrEnd>, an equally renowned <clr>primitivist artist<clrEnd>. And the third is a <clr>maloq by the name of B'Ugarra<clrEnd>. He represents the competition's sponsors - that's why he's on the judges' panel. He knows nothing about art, but, as a maloq, he likes <clr>colorful<clrEnd> paintings.
Do you have any more questions?" the peleng asks.
loc.2.3:
"The competition consists of three rounds. In each round you are given a task and must produce a painting to please the judges. They assess the value of each piece. These values are then added up to get a total score. The participant with the highest total score after three rounds is the winner!
You'll also be provided with different paints to choose from. <clr>Fluorescent paints<clrEnd> have an extraordinary glow in ultraviolet light and <clr>make your work original<clrEnd>. 
However, this diminishes its <clr>precision<clrEnd>. 
I must say that <clr>common paints<clrEnd> aren't that spectacular, but they do produce <clr>fine realistic pieces<clrEnd>.
You'll have <clr>one hour for each<clrEnd> task."
"More questions?" the peleng asks.
loc.2.4:
"<clr>Imagination<clrEnd> makes your painting <clr>extraordinary and original<clrEnd>. <clr>Cleanness<clrEnd> depends on your <clr>precision<clrEnd>. Your <clr>competence<clrEnd> is crucial to the <clr>composition and color<clrEnd> of your paintings." 
"Any more questions?" asks the peleng.
loc.2.5:
"I'm not very good at art, so I can only say one thing. Style is very important. Before drawing something, think about whether or not it fits the chosen style. For example, it's very difficult to draw a cubist tree an impressionistic gravicar. That's all, I believe."
"Questions?" the peleng asks.
loc.3.0: You have a good time at the nearest pub and fly away in the morning.
loc.5.0:
There is nothing interesting in the room. A wide bed sits in the middle with an old nightstand next to it. A middle-sized book with paintings on the cover lies on the nightstand. "Why, it's 'World Art History' - a galactic worstseller! It's forbidden on almost every maloq planet!" you exclaimed. "I must read it!"
Unfortunately, the stereovision is broken. The room is definitely not a deluxe suite. Since it's getting dark, you go to bed.
loc.7.0:
You wake up ready for battle of every kind, even artistic combat. As soon as you've dressed and eaten your breakfast, your guide knocks at the door and escorts you to the gravicar. A small group of shabby-looking journalists are waiting for you near the hotel exit. After answering some of their stupid questions, you finally take a seat in the gravicar. The trip is quite long, but in the end you stop at a huge building in the exhibition center. 
"And now I leave you!" says the peleng. "I'll take you home after your fail... err...I mean, your triumph. See ya." He leaves.
You make your way to the venue, following the signs that mark the way. You go the wrong way a couple of times, but somehow you manage to arrive before the competition begins. The hall where the competition will take place is rather large and has enormous windows. The lighting is very good. Humans and gaals make up most of the audience, but there are occasional representatives of the other races. The stage is right in front of you. The competition hasn't begun yet. 
You take a seat near one of the four easels. An assistant runs up to you and offers two kinds of paints: <clr>fluorescent paints<clrEnd> and <clr>common paints<clrEnd>.

...<clr>Primitivism<clrEnd> is imitation of primitive art, e.g. an intentional return to primitive forms... "It's like paintings by children. <clr>Extremely imprecise, but very extraordinary<clrEnd>." 

You've memorized a lot of terms, but you start to fear that your head is about to explode.

jump.254.desc: This topic isn't a good match to your painting style. Unfortunately, all your attempts to paint fail miserably.
jump.255.desc: This topic isn't a good match to your painting style. Unfortunately, all your attempts to paint fail miserably.
jump.257.text: Paint the head of one of your maternal aunts
jump.257.desc: You try to paint according to your plan, but what you produce doesn't look anything like the assigned theme. You end up with something that resembles a mating penchekryak rather than a head.
jump.258.desc: The dragon head looks terrible - it seems you've chosen the wrong style.
jump.259.text: Paint a teakettle instead of a head
jump.259.desc: The tea-kettle, which you faithfully painted in your chosen style, looks like a poor substitute for a headdress or a head. In any event, you fail to express your ideas.
jump.261.text: Paint a couple more heads instead of the body
jump.261.desc: Your style is too realistic to express all your ideas - you'll have to repaint everything. Unfortunately, the different layers of paint smear together, producing an repulsive, dirty grey color.
jump.262.text: Paint the body of a dragon
jump.262.desc: It is impossible to paint a dragon in the chosen style. The result is very strange. But that's not all - your composition leaves much to be desired.
jump.263.text: Draw the body of a coiled snake
jump.263.desc: Snake coils painted in the cubist style will always look grotesque and sloppy.
jump.264.text: Put the book down and go to sleep
jump.265.desc: You think it over and then mix a beautiful color that fits your work perfectly. You use it to fill in the background.
jump.266.desc: You spent the whole night reading and the result is evident - you've done your best and painted a wonderful landscape in the background, following all the rules of artistic composition.
jump.267.desc: Your time spent reading fantasy novels about space travel all night long was not in vain. You surrender the reins to your imagination and produce a wonderful picture of outerspace. It's full of mysterious stars and nebulae in a background that doesn't stand out too prominently to distract attention from your beast.
jump.268.desc: You try to imagine painting a fantastic landscape in the background, but it looks like what you might see in a state of delirium. However, the realism of your painting rivals photography.
jump.269.desc: You decide to fill the background with color. It turns out to be quite idyllic; it makes your beast look better by contrasting one color with another.
jump.270.desc: You paint creatively and the result is really outstanding!
jump.271.desc: You carefully paint according to your plan and achieve an almost photographic likeness!
jump.272.desc: You give full scope to your imagination and begin painting with vivid, clean colors. They blend together nicely and the result is enchanting.
jump.273.text: Paint the head of one of your maternal aunts
jump.273.desc: You succeed in rendering a very good likeness of the subject. Moreover, the painting has a twinge of humor to it. The red harmonizes nicely with the intensity of the whole piece.
jump.274.desc: The monster's head painted impressionistically looks marvelous.
jump.275.text: Paint a teakettle instead of a head
jump.275.desc: You paint a very realistic teakettle. It transitions seamlessly into the neck - a very original and even charming look.
jump.276.text: Paint a couple more heads instead of the body
jump.276.desc: Using your knowledge of anatomy, you draw terrifying - and very realistic - muzzles. The painting's general surrealist style really catches the eye.
jump.277.text: Paint the body of a dragon
jump.277.desc: The fanciful dragon's body is very precise, beautiful, and realistic. As an artist, you can really proud of this great work of art!
jump.278.text: Draw the body of a coiled snake
jump.278.desc: The classy coils look very original in your painting style. They are fantastic and harmonize well with the background.
jump.280.text: Paint a flight deck that looks like a gaalian destroyer
jump.280.desc: You try to depict a flight deck in your chosen style, but you just can't. After several failed attempts to repair your mistake, you choose the easy way out and simply paint some abstract flight deck.
jump.281.text: Paint the Klissan flight deck you've seen in the Gaaldock Museum
jump.281.desc: Primitivism is just not very well suited to painting such detailed objects. What you end up producing hardly resembles a flight deck. The colors are also wild and clashing.
jump.282.desc: It's almost impossible to paint something abstract and fantastic in the realistic style. And you fail when you tried. You produced a rather ordinary cabin that had been encroached upon with some strange and entirely impossible constructions.
jump.283.text: Paint a flight deck that looks like a gaalian destroyer
jump.283.desc: You begin to draw the cabin very precisely, considering the effects of lighting and shadows. Then you finish the cabin with enigmatic design. All in all is looks wonderful!
jump.284.text: Paint the Klissan flight deck you've seen in the Gaaldock Museum
jump.284.desc: A bit of surrealism combined with the familiar green steel design looks brilliant!
jump.285.desc: The surrealist style is a suitable match for an improvisation like this. In short order, a wonderful and fantastic cabin appears on your canvas.
jump.287.text: Remember how you used to paint ships as a child
jump.287.desc: You spend some time recollecting your childhood and eventually succeed in recreating your fantasies. The result is impressive!
jump.288.text: Remember how you used to paint ships as a child
jump.288.desc: You fail to realistically depict your childhood fantasies. You end up with a strange and badly-positioned figure that looks rather stupid.
jump.289.text: Paint some stylish stickers on the main hull
jump.289.desc: Your surreal wing design is a total success. And the color matches perfectly!
jump.290.text: Paint some stylish stickers on the main hull
jump.290.desc: You finally manage to create a curious design on the wings, but it looks a bit mangled and even a bit stupid. You have to repaint it, but the wet paints intermix and produce a dirty grey color.
jump.291.text: Paint the main part to look like an ancient stealth aircraft.
jump.291.desc: There is no possibility of painting a cubic form in the surrealistic style. You fail to produce anything decent.
jump.292.text: Paint the main part to look like an ancient stealth aircraft.
jump.292.desc: You've put for the effort and can now enjoy a perfect result.
jump.294.text: Paint wings that resemble those of the Faeyan Ranger Corps and add some other cool features
jump.294.desc: The wings painted in the primitivist style look very strange. The only thing that looks remotely faeyan about them is their color. But even the color doesn't really resemble the faeyan original violet color. It is offensively inky. You give up and are unable to repaint anything.
jump.295.text: Paint wings that resemble those of the Faeyan Ranger Corps and add some other cool features
jump.295.desc: The wings look very natural. The 	checkered light and shade is marvelous. That all-nighter of book reading was not in vain!
jump.296.desc: The beautiful and fantastic wings are in perfect harmony with the rest of the picture. They look very artistic. Even though the wings are shaped like those on a butterfly, they look like they are made of carbon.
jump.297.desc: The vivid wings spice up the painting a bit, but the iridescent paint kills all the other details and attracts too much attention to itself. Your precision also leaves much to be desired.
jump.298.text: Don't paint wings. Instead, paint an aggressive-looking hull with spikes on the bottom
jump.298.desc: Your creation is formidable and looks threatening. You are quite satisfied with the result.
jump.299.text: Don't paint wings. Instead, paint an aggressive-looking hull with spikes on the bottom
jump.299.desc: You really botched things up when working at the form of your painting. The poor quality paint made it impossible to fix the situation; they don't hide the bottom layers of paint.
jump.301.desc: You fail to paint outerspace in the surrealistic style. Although the background conforms to all the rules of the chosen style, it simply doesn't look like outerspace. You've also thought too much about which color to use.
jump.302.desc: Your impressionistic painting of outerspace looks very striking and interesting! The star in the background is especially impressive.
jump.303.text: Just do a careful wash of paint
jump.303.desc: Your cubist painting style harmonizes well with your professional color wash in the background. The background does not draw too much attention to itself, and it emphasizes the beauty of the foreground.
jump.304.text: Just do a careful wash of paint
jump.304.desc: Your vivid style does not go well with the boring and grey color of the background. Consequently, the background does not improve the painting at all.
jump.305.desc: The forest is impressive. It looks like a tropical jungle. Feeling inspired, you paint some ancient ruins in the picturesque background. The result is excellent!
jump.306.desc: You fail to paint the forest in a truly cubistic manner. The trees in the background look like odd spheres on thick legs. It makes the painting look more original, but your colors are a failure.
jump.313.text: Repaint the wings, guns, and other parts
jump.318.text: Repaint the facial contours, ears, hair, and so on
jump.319.text: Can you give me a piece of advice or some guidelines?
jump.337.text: Thanks, but I don't want any of these things.
jump.337.desc:
"Here's home sweet home. I'll drop by for you tomorrow," your guide says as he turns around.

The peleng takes you to his gravicar. It's an early model with a wide dent on the left side. One of the headlights is broken. He gives you a ride to a small motel in the suburbs. It's the place of choice for unlucky travelers whose vehicles break down on the road, as well as amorous couples seeking intimacy. The neon sign is rusty and flickering.  From time to time, it looks like the sign reads "Moth" instead of "Motel" - an honest warning to visitors of the potential dangers within. You go upstairs only to find a rundown room there.
